purpose: session_bounded_stepwise_execution_for_architectural_design_and_the_built_environment: a machine-readable expert-system KB whose nodes are concrete architectural-design work-units (form and space ordering, structure and context, representation, building types) usable for planning, evaluation, prioritization, conflict resolution, validation, and anti-rework workflow as a subdomain node of a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: DOMAIN is the architecture and built-environment subdomain of Design: Fashion, Architecture & Principles.
No observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Nodes are concrete architectural-design work-units, not generic design platitudes.
Proportion and geometry ties to the applied-math specialist for proportioning systems and grids.
Scope spans schematic design through coordinated documentation handoff, not site construction or contract administration.
exclusions: on-site construction execution and contract administration
detailed structural member calculation and connection design
interior decoration, furniture, and styling specifics
regional and statutory planning policy beyond the project's zoning and code envelope
landscape and civil infrastructure design beyond immediate site context

competency_questions.question: What must the building do, for whom, and on what budget and site before any form is drawn?
How does the design respond to the site's climate, orientation, access, and urban context?
What legal envelope, code, egress, and accessibility rules must the design satisfy to be permittable?
What organizing idea (parti) and spatial organization arrange the program?
How does circulation connect spaces and meet required adjacencies and human scale?
Which ordering principles and proportioning systems give the composition order?
How are proportion and geometry reconciled with human scale and clearances?
What structural system and load path support the chosen form and spans?
What materials and assemblies meet performance, durability, and intent?
How are daylight, envelope, and energy balanced for comfort and performance?
How is sustainability integrated passive-first rather than bolted on?
Which drawings (plan, section, elevation, perspective) communicate and coordinate the design?
What is the governing spatial concept and how is its hierarchy made legible?
How does building-type knowledge (residential, civic, urban) shape the design?

glossary.definition: the central organizing idea or diagram that governs a design's spatial order
a line, plane, or volume that gathers and orders other elements by reference
geometric lines that govern proportional relationships across a composition
the measurement of the human body used to size spaces and clearances
the continuous route by which loads travel through structure to the foundations
the assembly of walls, roof, and openings separating inside from outside
a path of higher heat flow that bypasses insulation in the envelope
a scaled projection (plan, section, elevation) with no perspective distortion
a vertical cut through a building showing heights, levels, and structure
greenhouse-gas emissions from making and constructing a building's materials
the spatial and signage logic that lets occupants find their way through a building
the shared outdoor space a building shapes at its street and edges

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established architectural-design literature (Ching, Architecture: Form, Space, and Order; Ching, Design Drawing) and standard practice in programming, site and code analysis, structure, building physics, sustainability, representation, and building types; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Fix what the building must do, for whom, on what budget and site, and the spatial program before any form is drawn.
contradictors: designer who forms before program

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the client requirements, budget, or program of spaces changes

pros.claim: every later form and structural decision inherits one clear program
pros.example: a clinic and a gallery need different adjacency even on the same footprint

cons.claim: a wrong or vague program misdirects the whole design
cons.example: sizing rooms before knowing required occupant counts

failure_modes: program stated as wishes not measurable areas
acceptance_tests: program lists every space with area and adjacency
objectives name measurable success criteria

nodes.definition: Read the site's geometry, climate, orientation, access, views, and surrounding fabric to define what the design must respond to.
contradictors: designer who ignores context

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the site, climate data, or surrounding context changes

pros.claim: the design is grounded in real orientation, climate, and context
pros.example: placing glazing to the daylit aspect and away from a noisy road

cons.claim: missing a constraint forces costly redesign late
cons.example: discovering a setback or easement after massing is fixed

failure_modes: sun path or prevailing wind misread
acceptance_tests: analysis names orientation, climate, access, and context constraints
each constraint maps to a design response

nodes.definition: Establish the legal envelope: zoning, setbacks, height, allowable area, occupancy, egress, and accessibility rules the design must satisfy.
contradictors: designer who treats code as an afterthought

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when zoning, code edition, occupancy, or accessibility requirements change

pros.claim: design stays permittable and avoids illegal massing
pros.example: confirming allowable height before designing a fourth storey

cons.claim: a code miss can void a permit and force redesign
cons.example: an egress width that fails occupant load late in design

failure_modes: wrong code edition or occupancy class used
acceptance_tests: buildable envelope reflects zoning and height limits
egress and accessibility requirements are documented

nodes.definition: Set the building's overall volume, footprint, and the organizing diagram (parti) that captures the central spatial idea.
contradictors: designer who skips a governing concept

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the program, envelope, or governing concept changes

pros.claim: a clear parti gives every later move a reason and coherence
pros.example: a courtyard parti that organizes circulation and daylight at once

cons.claim: a weak concept yields incoherent ad hoc spaces
cons.example: rooms added without a governing order

failure_modes: parti not legible in the plan
acceptance_tests: massing fits within the buildable envelope
one diagram explains the organizing idea

nodes.definition: Arrange spaces and the paths between them (linear, radial, clustered, grid) so the plan supports use, adjacency, and movement.
contradictors: designer who lays out rooms without circulation logic

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the program adjacency or organizing parti changes

pros.claim: movement and use flow logically from a chosen pattern
pros.example: a radial layout that centers a shared atrium

cons.claim: poor circulation wastes area and confuses users
cons.example: a corridor that forces backtracking between linked rooms

acceptance_tests: every program adjacency is satisfied or justified
circulation reaches all spaces without dead loops

nodes.definition: Apply form-and-space ordering devices (axis, symmetry, hierarchy, rhythm, repetition, datum, transformation) to give the composition order.
contradictors: designer who orders by intuition only

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the parti or compositional intent changes

pros.claim: ordering devices make the design legible and intentional
pros.example: a repeating bay rhythm that unifies a long facade

cons.claim: over-applied symmetry can fight program needs
cons.example: forcing a symmetric plan onto an asymmetric program

failure_modes: hierarchy unclear so all spaces read equal
acceptance_tests: a primary ordering device is named and applied
spatial hierarchy is legible in the plan

nodes.definition: Set proportioning systems and geometry (ratios, golden section, modular grids, regulating lines) that govern dimensions and relationships.
contradictors: designer who dimensions arbitrarily

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the module, grid, or proportioning system changes

pros.claim: consistent proportion ties scale and harmony across the building
pros.example: a 1.5 m planning module that coordinates rooms, structure, and facade

cons.claim: rigid geometry can waste space or fight site
cons.example: forcing a square grid onto an irregular plot

acceptance_tests: a proportioning or grid system is defined and used
key dimensions trace to the chosen system

nodes.definition: Calibrate spaces to human scale and anthropometrics so dimensions, heights, and clearances suit occupants and intended feeling.
contradictors: designer who ignores body dimensions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when occupancy, accessibility, or intended spatial feeling changes

pros.claim: spaces feel right and meet clearances for real bodies
pros.example: a ceiling height tuned to make a lobby feel generous yet efficient

cons.claim: wrong scale makes spaces cramped or cavernous
cons.example: a corridor too narrow for two-way accessible passing

failure_modes: monumental scale where intimacy is wanted
acceptance_tests: clearances meet accessibility minimums
heights and dimensions suit the intended use and feeling

nodes.definition: Choose a primary structural system and grid (load-bearing, frame, span strategy) compatible with form, spans, and loads.
contradictors: designer who fixes form without a load path

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when spans, loads, material strategy, or massing change

pros.claim: a coherent load path keeps the building standable and economical
pros.example: a regular column grid that frees an open ground floor

cons.claim: a structure forced late distorts the plan and cost
cons.example: adding transfer beams because the grid ignored a column-free space

failure_modes: no continuous load path to foundations
grid clashes with required clear spans
acceptance_tests: a continuous vertical load path is shown to the foundations
structural grid aligns with required spans

nodes.definition: Select materials and construction assemblies for structure, envelope, and finish that meet performance, durability, and intent.
contradictors: designer who picks materials by image alone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when structure, climate response, budget, or design intent changes

pros.claim: assemblies meet performance, durability, and look together
pros.example: a rainscreen build-up that drains and weathers well

cons.claim: a material chosen for image can fail in service
cons.example: a porous stone facing in a freeze-thaw climate

failure_modes: assembly lacks a drainage or vapor strategy
material incompatible with structure or climate
acceptance_tests: each assembly resolves structure, weather, and finish
materials suit the climate and budget

nodes.definition: Design the building envelope for insulation, airtightness, moisture control, and thermal performance against the climate.
contradictors: designer who treats the wall as a single layer

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when assemblies, climate, or orientation change

pros.claim: a controlled envelope cuts energy use and avoids condensation
pros.example: a continuous insulation and air barrier that stops thermal bridging

cons.claim: an envelope gap causes mold and heat loss
cons.example: an interrupted vapor control layer trapping moisture in the wall

failure_modes: thermal bridge or air leak path left in the build-up
vapor control on the wrong side
acceptance_tests: the envelope has a continuous insulation and air-control layer
the build-up manages moisture for the climate

nodes.definition: Plan glazing, apertures, and shading to bring useful daylight into spaces while controlling glare and solar gain.
contradictors: designer who glazes without solar study

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when orientation, plan, or climate data changes

pros.claim: good daylight improves comfort and cuts lighting energy
pros.example: north light for steady, glare-free studio illumination

cons.claim: unshaded glazing overheats and glares
cons.example: a west window that bakes the room each afternoon

failure_modes: solar gain or glare not controlled
acceptance_tests: each habitable space has a daylight strategy
glare and solar gain are addressed with shading

nodes.definition: Integrate passive strategies, energy performance, and lifecycle/embodied-carbon thinking into the design.
contradictors: designer who bolts on sustainability at the end

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when envelope, daylight, material, or energy targets change

pros.claim: passive-first design reduces energy demand before adding systems
pros.example: orientation and shading that cut cooling load without mechanical help

cons.claim: late add-on sustainability is costly and weak
cons.example: buying offsets instead of reducing demand by design

failure_modes: sustainability treated as a checklist not a strategy
embodied carbon ignored for operational only
acceptance_tests: passive strategies are integrated before systems
an energy and embodied-carbon target is stated

nodes.definition: Produce orthographic plans: scaled horizontal cuts showing layout, dimensions, walls, openings, and spatial relationships.
contradictors: designer who communicates only in sketches

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when layout, grid, or dimensions change

pros.claim: plans communicate layout precisely to all parties
pros.example: a dimensioned plan a builder can set out from

cons.claim: an inconsistent plan misleads construction
cons.example: a wall shown in plan that contradicts the section

acceptance_tests: plans are drawn to a stated scale with dimensions
plan agrees with section and elevation

nodes.definition: Produce sections and elevations: vertical cuts and orthographic faces showing heights, levels, envelope, and facade composition.
contradictors: designer who never cuts a section

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when plan, levels, structure, or envelope changes

pros.claim: sections reveal vertical space, light, and structure together
pros.example: a section that proves a double-height space clears the structure

cons.claim: a missing section hides vertical clashes
cons.example: a stair that fails headroom only visible in section

acceptance_tests: sections show levels, structure, and clearances
elevations match plan and section dimensions

nodes.definition: Construct perspective views and visualizations that communicate three-dimensional space, light, and experience to non-experts.
contradictors: designer who relies only on plans for clients

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when geometry, materials, or light strategy changes

pros.claim: perspectives let clients judge the real spatial experience
pros.example: an eye-level view that shows how a lobby will feel on entry

cons.claim: a flattering render can hide a real spatial problem
cons.example: a wide-angle view that disguises a cramped corridor

acceptance_tests: perspectives are constructed from the actual geometry
views represent real materials and light

nodes.definition: Apply residential building-type knowledge: dwelling units, privacy gradients, domestic program, and housing density patterns.
contradictors: designer applying civic logic to a home

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when dwelling program, density, or domestic privacy needs change

pros.claim: dwellings get a workable privacy gradient and unit mix
pros.example: separating sleeping zones from a shared living core

cons.claim: a generic layout ignores domestic life patterns
cons.example: a kitchen with no relation to dining or entry

failure_modes: public-building logic forced onto a dwelling
acceptance_tests: dwelling layout supports a sensible privacy gradient
unit types meet the program and code

nodes.definition: Apply public/civic building-type knowledge: large assembly, wayfinding, accessibility, durability, and civic presence.
contradictors: designer using domestic scale for civic crowds

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when occupancy, egress, or civic program changes

pros.claim: large public flows and wayfinding are handled deliberately
pros.example: a clear concourse that disperses a crowd to multiple halls

cons.claim: under-scaled egress or wayfinding endangers crowds
cons.example: a single exit choking a full assembly space

acceptance_tests: egress and accessibility meet the occupant load
wayfinding guides a first-time visitor

nodes.definition: Relate the building to its urban context: street edge, public realm, massing fit, and contribution to the surrounding fabric.
contradictors: designer who treats the building as an object on a plinth

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when context, massing, or zoning envelope changes

pros.claim: the building strengthens the street and public realm
pros.example: an active ground floor that animates the sidewalk

cons.claim: an object-building can deaden its street
cons.example: a blank wall facing a busy pedestrian route

failure_modes: building ignores street edge and scale of neighbors
public realm left as residual space
acceptance_tests: the design defines a positive street edge
massing fits the scale of its context

nodes.definition: Run the design review and assemble a coordinated, buildable documentation set as the validated handoff for construction.
contradictors: designer who issues uncoordinated drawings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any drawing, spec, or compliance item changes before issue

pros.claim: a coordinated set is buildable and avoids site clashes
pros.example: catching a duct that clashes with a beam before tender

cons.claim: an uncoordinated set causes expensive site rework
cons.example: drawings issued with plan and section dimensions disagreeing

failure_modes: code or accessibility item missed at issue
acceptance_tests: the set is internally coordinated across disciplines
code and accessibility compliance is recorded before issue

edges.why_related: the program defines what the site must be read against
edges.risk_of_conflict: reading the site without a program wastes effort
edges.example: analyzing access for a use not yet known
edges.resolution_rule: fix the program before site analysis

edges.why_related: the program drives the volume and organizing idea
edges.risk_of_conflict: massing without a program is arbitrary
edges.example: sizing a volume before knowing areas
edges.resolution_rule: fix the program before massing

edges.why_related: the site location sets which zoning and codes apply
edges.benefit_of_coupling: compliance is checked against the real jurisdiction
edges.risk_of_conflict: code without site context is generic
edges.example: applying the wrong jurisdiction's setbacks
edges.resolution_rule: resolve the site before code analysis

edges.why_related: orientation, views, and context shape the massing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: massing responds to climate and context
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the site distorts the massing
edges.example: facing glazing away from the daylit aspect
edges.resolution_rule: let the site analysis steer the massing

edges.why_related: zoning bounds the buildable height, area, and setbacks
edges.benefit_of_coupling: massing stays within the legal envelope
edges.risk_of_conflict: massing can exceed the envelope
edges.example: designing a storey above the height limit
edges.resolution_rule: keep massing within the buildable envelope; revise massing not the code

edges.why_related: the parti frames how spaces and paths are organized
edges.risk_of_conflict: organizing without a parti is incoherent
edges.example: corridors with no relation to the concept
edges.resolution_rule: fix the parti before detailed organization

edges.why_related: the organization is the substrate ordering devices act on
edges.risk_of_conflict: ordering applied to no layout is empty
edges.example: symmetry imposed before rooms exist
edges.resolution_rule: organize spaces before applying ordering devices

edges.why_related: ordering choices set up the proportioning and grid
edges.risk_of_conflict: proportion without ordering is arbitrary
edges.example: a grid with no compositional intent
edges.resolution_rule: choose ordering devices before fixing proportions

edges.why_related: the proportioning grid bounds achievable human dimensions
edges.risk_of_conflict: a grid can force inhuman dimensions
edges.example: a module that yields a too-low ceiling
edges.resolution_rule: human scale overrides a grid that breaks clearances

edges.why_related: the layout sets where human-scale clearances must hold
edges.benefit_of_coupling: scale is calibrated to real spaces
edges.risk_of_conflict: scale tuned with no layout is abstract
edges.example: sizing a corridor with no plan
edges.resolution_rule: organize spaces before calibrating human scale

edges.why_related: the massing and spans drive the structural system choice
edges.risk_of_conflict: structure forced onto fixed form distorts it
edges.example: needing transfer beams a clean grid would avoid
edges.resolution_rule: co-develop massing and structure; massing leads, structure validates

edges.why_related: the planning grid constrains the structural grid and spans
edges.risk_of_conflict: an aesthetic grid can fight viable spans
edges.example: a column spacing that overspans the slab
edges.resolution_rule: reconcile planning and structural grids; spans govern where they conflict

edges.why_related: the structure determines compatible materials and assemblies
edges.risk_of_conflict: materials chosen against the structure fail
edges.example: a heavy facade on a frame sized for light cladding
edges.resolution_rule: select structure before fixing material assemblies

edges.why_related: the chosen assemblies define the envelope build-up
edges.benefit_of_coupling: envelope performance flows from the assembly
edges.risk_of_conflict: an envelope spec with no assembly is hollow
edges.example: specifying insulation with no wall build-up
edges.resolution_rule: define assemblies before envelope performance

edges.why_related: climate and orientation change the envelope demands
edges.benefit_of_coupling: envelope is tuned to the real climate
edges.risk_of_conflict: a generic envelope underperforms locally
edges.example: the same wall in tropical and arctic climates
edges.resolution_rule: let climate analysis drive envelope targets

edges.why_related: orientation and sun path govern daylight strategy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: apertures respond to the real sun path
edges.risk_of_conflict: glazing placed without sun study overheats
edges.example: a west wall of glass with no shading
edges.resolution_rule: let the sun-path analysis drive daylighting

edges.why_related: the plan depth determines where daylight can reach
edges.risk_of_conflict: deep-plan rooms get no daylight
edges.example: an internal room with no borrowed light
edges.resolution_rule: organize spaces before fixing the daylight plan

edges.why_related: more glazing for daylight worsens thermal performance
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbalanced glazing overheats or darkens
edges.example: floor-to-ceiling glass that ruins the thermal envelope
edges.resolution_rule: optimize glazing ratio and shading; thermal limits cap glazing where they conflict

edges.why_related: envelope performance is the basis of energy strategy
edges.benefit_of_coupling: energy targets build on the envelope
edges.risk_of_conflict: an energy plan without an envelope is empty
edges.example: claiming low energy with a leaky envelope
edges.resolution_rule: fix the envelope before energy strategy

edges.why_related: daylight reduces electric lighting and shapes loads
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring daylight raises energy use
edges.example: lighting a daylit room artificially all day
edges.resolution_rule: integrate daylight into the energy strategy

edges.why_related: material choices drive embodied carbon and lifecycle impact
edges.risk_of_conflict: high-carbon materials undercut energy gains
edges.example: a carbon-heavy structure offsetting operational savings
edges.resolution_rule: weigh embodied against operational; reduce embodied where it dominates

edges.why_related: the organizational plan is what the drawing documents
edges.risk_of_conflict: drawing with no layout is meaningless
edges.example: dimensioning a plan that has no resolved rooms
edges.resolution_rule: resolve organization before producing plan drawings

edges.why_related: the dimensional grid governs the plan's setting-out
edges.risk_of_conflict: a plan off the grid misaligns construction
edges.example: walls dimensioned off the planning module
edges.resolution_rule: draw plans to the agreed dimensional grid

edges.why_related: sections and elevations are cut from the plan
edges.risk_of_conflict: sections drawn without a plan diverge
edges.example: a section level that contradicts the plan
edges.resolution_rule: fix plans before sections and elevations

edges.why_related: the structure sets heights and depths shown in section
edges.risk_of_conflict: a section ignoring structure misleads
edges.example: a ceiling that ignores the beam depth
edges.resolution_rule: show actual structure in sections

edges.why_related: orthographic drawings provide the geometry for perspectives
edges.benefit_of_coupling: perspectives are built from real geometry
edges.risk_of_conflict: perspectives without orthographics distort
edges.example: a render that disagrees with the elevation
edges.resolution_rule: build perspectives from the orthographic set

edges.why_related: human-scale clearances bound the dimensioned plan
edges.risk_of_conflict: a plan can ignore accessible clearances
edges.example: a door clearance below the accessible minimum
edges.resolution_rule: plans must respect human-scale clearances

edges.why_related: type-specific dwelling logic builds on the organization
edges.benefit_of_coupling: residential layouts inherit a circulation logic
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying a type with no organization fails
edges.example: privacy zones with no circulation plan
edges.resolution_rule: organize spaces before applying residential type

edges.why_related: domestic spaces depend on human-scale calibration
edges.benefit_of_coupling: dwellings feel right at human scale
edges.risk_of_conflict: unscaled dwellings feel wrong
edges.example: a living room sized like a hall
edges.resolution_rule: calibrate scale before residential layout

edges.why_related: civic assembly and wayfinding build on the organization
edges.benefit_of_coupling: public flows inherit a circulation logic
edges.risk_of_conflict: a civic type with no organization fails
edges.example: an assembly hall with no concourse plan
edges.resolution_rule: organize spaces before applying civic type

edges.why_related: occupancy and egress code bound civic assembly design
edges.benefit_of_coupling: civic design stays within egress limits
edges.risk_of_conflict: under-sized egress endangers crowds
edges.example: one exit for a packed hall
edges.resolution_rule: egress code governs civic assembly sizing

edges.why_related: the massing is what meets the street and context
edges.benefit_of_coupling: urban response builds on the massing
edges.risk_of_conflict: an urban strategy with no massing is empty
edges.example: a street edge with no resolved volume
edges.resolution_rule: fix massing before the urban-realm interface

edges.why_related: the context reading defines the urban response
edges.benefit_of_coupling: urban fit follows the context analysis
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring context produces an alien object
edges.example: a blank wall on an active street
edges.resolution_rule: ground the urban response in the context analysis

edges.why_related: monumental ordering can clash with intimate human scale
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-ordering dwarfs the occupant
edges.example: a grand symmetry that dwarfs a small lobby
edges.resolution_rule: human scale tempers ordering where they conflict

edges.why_related: the plan set feeds the coordinated documentation
edges.risk_of_conflict: reviewing incomplete plans misses clashes
edges.example: issuing before plans are dimensioned
edges.resolution_rule: complete plans before the documentation review

edges.why_related: sections and elevations feed the coordinated set
edges.risk_of_conflict: missing sections hide vertical clashes
edges.example: a stair clash visible only in section
edges.resolution_rule: complete sections before documentation review

edges.why_related: the structure must be coordinated in the issued set
edges.risk_of_conflict: uncoordinated structure causes site rework
edges.example: a duct route clashing with a beam
edges.resolution_rule: coordinate structure before issuing documents

edges.why_related: energy and sustainability decisions must be captured before issue
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the set records the sustainability strategy
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unrecorded strategy is lost at handoff
edges.example: energy targets missing from the issued set
edges.resolution_rule: record the sustainability strategy before issue

conflict_axes.trigger: more glazing for daylight degrades the thermal envelope
resolution_order: set the daylight target per space
cap glazing to the thermal budget
add shading and high-performance glass
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: thermal limits cap glazing where energy targets are binding; otherwise daylight leads with shading
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if neither glazing nor shading can hold both comfort and energy target
conflict_axes.example: a south facade where full glazing would blow the cooling budget

conflict_axes.trigger: the desired form needs spans or cantilevers that are uneconomical
resolution_order: test the form against viable spans
adjust the grid or form
accept added structure only if the form is essential
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: structural feasibility governs; the form is adjusted unless the gesture is the project's core idea and budget allows
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the form requires transfer structure beyond budget
conflict_axes.example: a column-free hall that forces deep transfer beams

conflict_axes.trigger: monumental symmetry or rhythm dwarfs the occupant
resolution_order: check key spaces at eye level
temper the ordering device
preserve human clearances
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: human scale and clearances override ordering where they conflict
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if ordering forces clearances below accessible minimums
conflict_axes.example: a grand axis that leaves an intimate room feeling cavernous

conflict_axes.trigger: a striking massing ignores the scale and edge of its context
resolution_order: read the context scale and edges
fit the massing to the street
allow contrast only where the brief warrants
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: contextual fit and a positive street edge govern unless the brief explicitly seeks an iconic landmark
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the massing deadens an active street
conflict_axes.example: a blank-walled object set back from a lively sidewalk

resolution_order: estimate both embodied and operational carbon
minimize the dominant term over the lifecycle
prefer low-impact materials where operational gains are small
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: reduce whichever term dominates over the building lifecycle; do not trade large embodied carbon for small operational gains
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a carbon-heavy structure is justified only by minor operational savings
conflict_axes.example: thick concrete mass added for marginal thermal benefit

conflict_axes.trigger: a rigid grid or pure geometry wastes program area or breaks adjacency
resolution_order: verify program areas and adjacencies
relax the grid where it wastes space
keep geometry only where it serves the program
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: program function governs; geometric purity yields where it harms required areas or adjacencies
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a pure grid leaves required spaces undersized
conflict_axes.example: a square module that leaves an awkward unusable remainder

conflict_axes.trigger: open circulation conflicts with required privacy or acoustic separation
resolution_order: map the privacy gradient
place buffers and doors at thresholds
keep openness only in shared zones
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: required privacy and acoustic separation govern in private zones; openness is preserved in shared zones
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if openness exposes a private function to a public path
conflict_axes.example: a bedroom opening directly onto a shared circulation spine

conflict_axes.trigger: a design move violates height, setback, egress, or accessibility rules
resolution_order: identify the binding code requirement
revise the design to comply
seek a variance only with client and authority
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: code compliance governs absolutely; the design is revised, not the code, unless a formal variance is granted
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: any unresolved code or accessibility violation at issue
conflict_axes.example: a cantilever that breaches the required setback

edge_cases.trigger: a code or accessibility breach is found after massing is fixed
edge_cases.failure_mode: the permit is refused and massing must be redesigned
edge_cases.example: a fourth storey that exceeds the height limit
edge_cases.detection_method: check the buildable envelope against zoning and code before locking massing

edge_cases.trigger: the form has no continuous load path to the foundations
edge_cases.failure_mode: the design is not buildable as drawn
edge_cases.example: a floating volume with no support shown
edge_cases.detection_method: trace every vertical load to a foundation on the structural diagram

edge_cases.trigger: plan and section dimensions or levels disagree
edge_cases.failure_mode: construction is set out from inconsistent drawings
edge_cases.example: a floor-to-floor height that differs between drawings
edge_cases.detection_method: cross-check shared dimensions across plan, section, and elevation
resolution: reconcile to one source of truth

edge_cases.trigger: the envelope build-up leaves a thermal bridge or air-leak path
edge_cases.failure_mode: condensation, mold, and heat loss in service
edge_cases.example: a slab edge that bypasses the insulation line
edge_cases.detection_method: trace the continuous insulation and air-control layers around every junction
resolution: close the bridge with continuous insulation

edge_cases.trigger: unshaded glazing causes glare and solar overheating
edge_cases.failure_mode: occupant discomfort and excess cooling load
edge_cases.example: a west window that bakes the room each afternoon
edge_cases.detection_method: check each aperture against the sun path for shading

edge_cases.trigger: spaces are added until the organizing idea is no longer legible
edge_cases.failure_mode: an incoherent plan with no governing order
edge_cases.example: rooms accreted around a courtyard until the court is buried
edge_cases.detection_method: test whether one diagram still explains the plan
resolution: remove or subordinate ad hoc spaces

edge_cases.trigger: a clearance falls below the accessible minimum
edge_cases.failure_mode: the space is non-compliant and unusable for some occupants
edge_cases.example: a corridor too narrow for two-way wheelchair passing
edge_cases.detection_method: check clearances against the accessibility standard on the plan

edge_cases.trigger: documents are issued with unresolved discipline clashes
edge_cases.failure_mode: expensive rework and delay on site
edge_cases.example: a duct route clashing with a structural beam
edge_cases.detection_method: run a coordination review across disciplines before issue

edge_cases.trigger: a visualization shows a space better than the real geometry allows
edge_cases.failure_mode: client expectations diverge from the buildable design
edge_cases.example: a wide-angle view that disguises a cramped corridor
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the perspective is built from the actual orthographic geometry
resolution: rebuild the view from real geometry

edge_cases.trigger: a setback, easement, or access constraint is discovered after massing
edge_cases.failure_mode: massing must be cut back and redesigned
edge_cases.example: an easement crossing the chosen footprint
edge_cases.detection_method: reconcile the massing footprint against the full site analysis
resolution: pull the massing off the constraint

workflow.objective: fix the program, budget, and design objectives
acceptance_tests: program lists every space with area and adjacency
objectives are measurable
workflow.do_first_because: nothing downstream is valid unless the program and budget are fixed first

workflow.objective: read the site and establish the legal buildable envelope
acceptance_tests: site constraints and orientation documented
buildable envelope and egress requirements recorded
exit_criteria: site analysis and legal envelope fixed
workflow.do_first_because: form must be developed inside a known site and legal envelope to avoid late redesign

workflow.objective: set the organizing idea, massing, and spatial organization
acceptance_tests: massing fits the buildable envelope
one diagram explains the organizing idea
workflow.do_first_because: the concept governs every later spatial and structural move

workflow.objective: apply ordering, proportion, and human scale to the composition
acceptance_tests: a primary ordering and proportioning system is applied
clearances meet accessible minimums
workflow.do_first_because: composition and scale must be set before structure and drawings inherit dimensions

workflow.objective: choose the structural system and material assemblies
acceptance_tests: a continuous load path reaches the foundations
each assembly resolves structure, weather, and finish
workflow.do_first_because: structure and material constrain envelope, drawings, and cost downstream

workflow.objective: resolve envelope, daylight, and energy performance
acceptance_tests: the envelope has continuous insulation and air control
each space has a daylight strategy and an energy target is set
workflow.do_first_because: performance must be integrated before documentation, not bolted on after

workflow.objective: apply building-type and urban-context knowledge to the design
acceptance_tests: the layout suits the building type's logic
the design defines a positive street edge
workflow.do_first_because: type and context refine the design before it is documented

workflow.objective: produce the coordinated orthographic drawing set
acceptance_tests: plans, sections, and elevations are drawn to scale
shared dimensions agree across drawings
workflow.do_first_because: a consistent orthographic set is the basis for visualization and documentation

acceptance_tests: perspectives are built from the real geometry
views represent real materials and light
workflow.do_first_because: visuals communicate the validated design to non-experts before sign-off

workflow.objective: review, coordinate, and issue the buildable documentation set
acceptance_tests: the set is internally coordinated across disciplines
code and accessibility compliance is recorded before issue
exit_criteria: documentation reviewed, compliant, and approved to issue
workflow.do_first_because: hard lock and issue are only valid after coordination, compliance, and human review pass

priority_rationale.notes: layout substrate for ordering and drawings
load path constrains materials and drawings
relates building to its street and fabric

dominance_rules.trigger: a design move conflicts with code, egress, or accessibility
dominance_rules.rule: code and accessibility compliance dominate over aesthetic preference
dominance_rules.required_action: revise the design to comply or obtain a formal variance
dominance_rules.example: trimming a cantilever that breaches the setback

dominance_rules.trigger: the desired form lacks a viable economical structure
dominance_rules.rule: structural feasibility dominates unless the gesture is the project's core idea and budget allows
dominance_rules.required_action: adjust the form or grid to a buildable structure
dominance_rules.example: reducing a span the budget cannot frame

dominance_rules.rule: human scale and accessible clearances dominate over ordering devices
dominance_rules.required_action: temper the ordering device to hold clearances
dominance_rules.example: widening a monumental corridor to an accessible clearance

dominance_rules.trigger: geometric purity wastes program area or breaks adjacency
dominance_rules.rule: program function dominates over geometric purity
dominance_rules.required_action: relax the grid where it harms required areas or adjacencies
dominance_rules.example: breaking a square module to recover usable area

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value step is unblocked but its prerequisite is unresolved
dominance_rules.rule: dependency precedence dominates over value-first ordering
dominance_rules.required_action: resolve the prerequisite before advancing the dependent step
dominance_rules.example: fixing the buildable envelope before detailing massing

dominance_rules.trigger: sustainability is deferred to the end of design
dominance_rules.rule: integrated passive performance dominates over late add-on measures
dominance_rules.required_action: resolve envelope, daylight, and energy before documentation
dominance_rules.example: orienting and shading before adding mechanical capacity

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates over automated progress for high-risk or irreversible decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: escalate to human review before locking or issuing
dominance_rules.example: a go/no-go before issuing the documentation set

dominance_rules.trigger: a step is ready to lock but coordination checks are incomplete
dominance_rules.rule: coordination QA dominates over locking on schedule
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the coordination review before any hard lock
dominance_rules.example: holding issue until a beam-duct clash is resolved

dominance_rules.trigger: a striking massing deadens its street or breaks context scale
dominance_rules.rule: contextual fit and a positive street edge dominate unless the brief seeks a landmark
dominance_rules.required_action: fit the massing to the street unless an iconic intent is briefed
dominance_rules.example: activating a ground floor instead of a blank wall

dominance_rules.trigger: drawings can be issued faster by skipping cross-checks
dominance_rules.rule: orthographic consistency dominates over issuing speed
dominance_rules.required_action: reconcile plan, section, and elevation before issue
dominance_rules.example: reconciling a floor-to-floor height across drawings before issue

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the program and budget before generating any form
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a form for the wrong program is reworked wholesale
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: massing changes after the program is clarified
anti_rework_rules.example: sizing rooms before occupant counts are known

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish the buildable envelope before fixing massing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: massing outside the legal envelope must be redesigned
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: massing exceeds height or setback limits
anti_rework_rules.example: designing a storey above the height limit

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete site and context analysis before committing massing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a missed site constraint forces late footprint redesign
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a setback or easement found after massing
anti_rework_rules.example: an easement crossing the chosen footprint

anti_rework_rules.rule: set the parti before detailed spatial organization
anti_rework_rules.rationale: organizing without a governing idea yields incoherent rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: circulation has no relation to the concept
anti_rework_rules.example: corridors added with no organizing logic

anti_rework_rules.rule: choose the structural system before fixing material assemblies
anti_rework_rules.rationale: materials chosen against the structure are reworked
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a facade weight the frame cannot carry
anti_rework_rules.example: heavy cladding on a frame sized for light panels

anti_rework_rules.rule: define material assemblies before envelope performance
anti_rework_rules.rationale: an envelope spec without a build-up is empty and re-derived
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: insulation specified with no wall build-up
anti_rework_rules.example: a performance target with no assembly to deliver it

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve envelope, daylight, and energy before documentation
anti_rework_rules.rationale: late performance changes ripple through the whole drawing set
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: energy or envelope changes after drawings start
anti_rework_rules.example: re-glazing a facade after sections are drawn

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve plans before sections and elevations
anti_rework_rules.rationale: sections cut from unresolved plans diverge and are redrawn
anti_rework_rules.example: a section height that disagrees with the plan

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the orthographic set before building perspectives
anti_rework_rules.rationale: visuals built on changing geometry are redone repeatedly
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a render disagrees with the elevation
anti_rework_rules.example: a perspective that contradicts the drawn facade

anti_rework_rules.rule: coordinate and review before any hard lock or issue
anti_rework_rules.rationale: issuing uncoordinated documents causes costly site rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a clash or code item found after issue
anti_rework_rules.example: a duct clashing with a beam discovered on site

iteration_protocol.trigger: the validator or a design review reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report checks and review notes to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and irreversibility
action: score by risk and rework cost
acceptance_tests: highest-risk defects are addressed first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue is empty or only low-risk warnings remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents through edges and dependencies
acceptance_tests: all dependents of a change are identified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: map the failure type to a repair subsystem
acceptance_tests: the fix resolves the failing check

iteration_protocol.trigger: a repair or a change to a locked or high-coupling node is made
iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and affected acceptance tests
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or a measured outcome would shift a node's importance
iteration_protocol.detection: compare proposed posterior change to the revisit delta
acceptance_tests: posterior recomputed from the formula
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior change is below the revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changes after a downstream lock
iteration_protocol.detection: detect a changed dependency of a locked node
acceptance_tests: no dependent stays locked on a changed prerequisite
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: all dependents are consistent with upstream state

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
iteration_protocol.detection: a defect exceeds the human-review risk threshold
acceptance_tests: a human decision is recorded before issue
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: the human decision is recorded and accepted

human_review_required_for: hard lock of the issued document set
resolution of any unresolved code violation

checks.repair_action: modeled daylight/thermal, form/structure, order/scale, embodied/operational tensions as conflict edges, not dependencies
recomputed all derived node and edge fields from the schema formulas

increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade on a failed coordination review
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
